products.name: Aether One
products.blurb: Closed-back planar headphones, tuned in a treated room. Memory-foam seals. Forty-two hours of unhurried listening.

products.name: Aether Drift
products.blurb: A compact in-ear pair with a matte case that disappears in a pocket. Tuned for speech and night records alike.

products.name: Aether Field
products.blurb: A cylindrical field speaker with a fabric grille and a low, even throw. Made to sit at the edge of a table and be forgotten.

products.name: Aether Halo
products.blurb: An arched desk lamp in milled aluminum. The head is a thin ring. The light is a pool, not a beam.

products.name: Aether Meridian
products.blurb: A 40 mm automatic with a dark dial and no numerals. The strap is unsealed leather. It is meant to mark hours, not announce them.

products.name: Aether Type
products.blurb: A low-profile 75% board in dark aluminum. Switches are chosen for a short, dry travel. No lights in the keys.

products.name: Aether Vessel
products.blurb: A dark-fired ceramic vessel for quiet scent. The mist is slow. The form is a bottle that never needed a label.

products.name: Aether Arc
products.blurb: A compact condenser on a small stand. Voiced for speech at a desk, with a grille that does not catch the light.

products.name: Nova Pro Wireless
products.blurb: A closed-back wireless instrument with a wide, even seal. Forty hours, a quiet microphone, and a graphite cup that does not catch the light.

products.name: AeroSound X
products.blurb: A slimmer over-ear with brushed dark-metal yokes. Built for long days at a desk and short walks between them.

products.name: Pulse Max
products.blurb: Deeper cups and a thicker band for listeners who want isolation without a clenched fit. Tuned a little warmer than the rest of the line.

products.name: Echo Studio
products.blurb: A straight-band studio pair with a dark coiled cable. Voiced flat enough to mix on, quiet enough to live with.

products.name: Void Elite
products.blurb: Faceted cups in graphite. A more private listen — the outside world recedes without being crushed.

products.name: Sonic Air Pro
products.blurb: A thin-band over-ear that almost forgets it is on. Made for travel days and late notes.

products.name: Phantom ANC
products.blurb: The quietest seal in the catalog. Thick pads, a midnight cup, and a microphone that does not announce itself.

products.name: Wave Pro
products.blurb: A dark mesh cup that lets a room remain a room. For evening records, not the train.

products.name: Apex Smart Watch
products.blurb: A squarer case in matte titanium-black. A dark face, a fluoroelastomer strap, and a week of quiet timekeeping.

products.name: Nova Watch X
products.blurb: A round case with a slim leather strap. Closer to a watch than a device — on purpose.

products.name: Pulse Watch Pro
products.blurb: A sport watch that still sits quietly on a wrist. Perforated strap, dual-frequency GPS, no spectacle.

products.name: Titan S
products.blurb: A larger, heavier case for people who knock into the world. Still matte. Still dark.

products.name: Orbit Watch
products.blurb: The thinnest instrument we keep. A milanese mesh strap and a case that disappears under a cuff.

products.name: Chrono X
products.blurb: A hybrid chronograph with dark subdials. Hands for the hour, a quiet sensor for the rest.

products.name: Vanta Watch
products.blurb: A case finished to swallow light. No polish, no bevel that winks. Just the hour.

products.name: Aero Fit Pro
products.blurb: A narrow fitness watch for people who do not want a slab on the wrist. Two weeks, then a short charge.

products.name: Mechanical Keyboard
products.blurb: A full-size board in dark aluminum. Tactile switches, no lights in the legends. The standard instrument.

products.name: Nova K87
products.blurb: Tenkeyless, gasket-mounted, a quieter bottom-out. Made to sit beside a notebook and not compete with it.

products.name: Phantom RGB
products.blurb: Named for light it does not insist on. South-facing LEDs stay off unless you ask. A compact 75% in charcoal.

products.name: Titan Mechanical
products.blurb: A denser board. Brass weight in the case, a sound that is short and dry. It does not slide.

products.name: Pulse 75
products.blurb: A 75% with a low front edge and a dark PBT set. For people who want arrows without the extra row.

products.name: Aero K65
products.blurb: Sixty-five percent. Arrows kept, bulk discarded. A travel board that still feels like a tool.

products.name: Vortex Pro
products.blurb: The flagship compact. Hand-assembled plate, tuned foam stack, a finish that does not fingerprint easily.

products.name: Shadow TKL
products.blurb: A darker TKL with quiet tactile switches. For shared rooms and late hours.

products.name: Gaming Mouse
products.blurb: A simple dark mouse. Light enough to forget, dense enough to aim. No lights required.

products.name: Nova Mouse Pro
products.blurb: Wireless without a brick in the palm. A matte shell that does not shine under a lamp.

products.name: Phantom X
products.blurb: Fifty-one grams without a honeycomb. Solid top, hollow interior, a quiet click.

products.name: Pulse Wireless
products.blurb: A slightly fuller wireless mouse for longer sessions. 4K polling when you want it, a day when you do not.

products.name: Titan Gaming Mouse
products.blurb: A deeper ergo curve. For palms that do not like a flat brick. Still matte, still dark.

products.name: Aero Mouse
products.blurb: A smaller mouse for smaller hands and quieter bags. The same sensor as its larger siblings.

products.name: Vortex Pro Mouse
products.blurb: The flagship mouse. 8K polling, a coated shell, and a charge that lasts a working week.

products.name: Shadow X
products.blurb: An ultra-matte shell that refuses fingerprints. Currently between lots — the next run is spoken for.

products.name: Runner X Sneakers
products.blurb: A dark road shoe with a quiet midsole. Built to disappear on pavement, not to photograph well from a mile away.

products.name: Nova Street
products.blurb: A low court shape in graphite leather. For days that are not about a split.

products.name: Aero Runner
products.blurb: Lighter than the X, a little quicker off the ground. Still black. Still quiet.

products.name: Phantom Runner
products.blurb: More foam, same refusal of loud colorways. A long-run shoe that does not look like a toy.

products.name: Urban X
products.blurb: A city shoe with a darker gumless outsole. Stands up to weather without asking for attention.

products.name: Velocity Pro
products.blurb: A plated racer in midnight. Reserved for days you mean it — and still unwilling to glow.

products.name: Shadow Runner
products.blurb: A trail shoe with a low, dark lugged sole. For paths that do not need to be announced.

products.name: Pulse Sneakers
products.blurb: A stable trainer for mixed days. Wider base, matte knit, no contrast flash.

products.name: Portable Speaker
products.blurb: A small dark cylinder for tables that already have enough objects. Twelve hours, a decent voice.

products.name: Nova Boom
products.blurb: A wider oval speaker with a stereo pair inside. Still small enough to carry by the hidden handle.

products.name: Pulse Sound
products.blurb: A pebble form that sits low. More midrange than bass-theatre. For kitchens and windowsills.

products.name: Aero Speaker Pro
products.blurb: A taller column with a cleaner throw. Twenty hours, a line-in for rooms that still have wires.

products.name: Titan Bass
products.blurb: The heaviest portable we keep. Dual passives, a darker voicing, still unwilling to look like a nightclub.

products.name: Wave X
products.blurb: A pairable stereo brick. Buy one, or two, and let them sit at either end of a table.

products.name: Phantom Speaker
products.blurb: A matte monolith, slightly larger than a book. Long battery, a voice that does not shout.

products.name: Sonic Boom Mini
products.blurb: The smallest speaker in the house. A pocket cylinder for travel days. Currently between lots.

products.name: Smart Band X
products.blurb: A thin band for people who do not want a watch. Sleep, heart, a silent alarm.

products.name: Wireless Charger Pro
products.blurb: A single dark disc. Fifteen watts, a felt pad, a cable that leaves out the back.

products.name: MagSafe Dock
products.blurb: A standing magnetic dock in milled aluminum. Phone upright, cable hidden, nothing glowing.

products.name: Smart Tracker
products.blurb: A charcoal coin for keys and cases. One year, a quiet chime, no loud logo.

products.name: USB-C Hub Pro
products.blurb: A dense little bar: HDMI, two USB-A, SD, a pass-through that does not get warm for no reason.

products.name: Premium Power Bank
products.blurb: Ten thousand milliamp-hours in a dark aluminum slab. Thirty watts out, a single button, no screen.

products.name: Desk Charging Station
products.blurb: Phone, watch, and buds on one dark tray. Cables leave through the back. The desk stays a desk.

products.name: Wireless Charging Pad
products.blurb: The thinnest pad we make. Ten watts, a leatherette top, almost flush to the table.

articles.title: On listening in rooms that forget you
articles.excerpt: A treated room is not an absence of sound. It is a decision about what is allowed to remain.
body: Most rooms insist. They clap back, they brighten the high notes, they make a voice sound like it is standing in a kitchen. We began Nexora by sitting in rooms that did the opposite — rooms that forgot you were there.

The One was voiced in such a room. Not to impress a measurement, but to make a record feel like it had been placed on the table, not thrown at the wall. Planar drivers helped. Silence in the seal helped more.
If an instrument is doing its work, you stop naming it. That is the only test we keep.

articles.title: Graphite, oxide, and the refusal of shine
articles.excerpt: Three finishes. No seasonal colours. A small argument against objects that perform their newness.
body: Shine is a kind of shouting. It photographs well and ages badly. We mill aluminum and leave it graphite. We darken steel until it reads as shadow. Oxide is the warmest of the three — a brown that is almost not a colour.
Midnight is not black. Black on a screen is a void. Midnight still has a temperature. Hold it near a window and it will admit a little blue.
We will not add a fourth finish because a calendar asked us to.
